# metais

A `.metais` file is a METAIS package: a document template. It declares
the inputs a document needs, each with a JSON Schema and a guide to what
it means, and renders the document from them. The `metais` command reads
it, checks inputs against it and renders it.

## Rules

- **Read a package with `metais`, in place.** Never unzip it, never read
  its raw bytes, never `cat` its README. Every command below takes the
  `.metais` file, or a source directory, as it is.
- **Never invent facts for a real document.** The inputs come from the
  person or from the sources they name. A value nobody supplied is asked
  for, not guessed, and not filled with a placeholder.
- **Fictional data only when the person asks for it** ("example data",
  "sample", "demo", "a preview"). Then generate it with
  `metais render <package> --sample` or `metais sample`; never copy a
  package's examples, and never hand-write placeholder values. An example
  is the author's illustration of the inputs, not the person's data.
- **Follow `next`.** Every command ends with the commands to run next
  (`Next:` in text, `next` in JSON). `<package>`, `<dir>` and `<data dir>`
  there are placeholders for your own paths.

## Filling in and rendering a package

1. `metais inspect report.metais` — what the package is, its guide, every
   input (with the file name it takes in a data directory, such as
   `status.json`), every output, and "Read next". Read all of it. If the
   guide was cut, `metais inspect report.metais --guide`.
2. Run what "Read next" lists, in order:
   - `metais read report.metais <entry>` for each input's meaning document;
   - `metais grep report.metais <pattern> references/` for the references.
3. `metais schema report.metais <input> --fields` — the fields of one
   input, one line each: its pointer (as `--set` takes it), its type,
   `required` or `optional`, its constraints and its title. Read it whole.
   A line that ends `when …` applies only under that condition, such as a
   field another field's value makes required. With no input it lists
   every input's fields; with `--json` they are `result.fields`. Only
   after it, for a field's description, read the whole schema:
   `metais schema report.metais <input>`, or write it to a file with
   `> <input>.schema.json`. Never dig fields out of its `$defs`: the
   listing has already followed every `$ref`.
4. Write a data directory: one file per input, named as `inspect` shows
   (`<input>.json`, `<input>.csv`, …), or one directory per collection
   input. `metais help inputs` explains `--set` and `--inputs-json`, which
   supply values on the command line instead.
5. `metais validate report.metais --data <data dir>` — every finding at
   once. Fix them all and run it again until it is clean.
6. `metais render report.metais --data <data dir> --out <new dir>` — the
   document. `--out` must be a new or empty directory; `--dry-run` lists
   what it would write.

**Fictional data, when asked for:**
`metais render report.metais --sample --out <new dir>` renders an example
of the document from generated data, in one step.
`metais sample report.metais --out <data dir>` writes valid generated data
to start from (`--seed <n>` varies it); then `validate` and `render` as
above. Say in your answer that the data is fictional. Never use generated
data for a real document.

## Writing a package

1. `metais init <dir> --minimal` — a new source directory with one input
   and one template to replace; without `--minimal`, a greeting with an
   example to learn from. Add `--html` for an HTML output: it declares
   `escape: html`, and its template writes data into a `<script>` with
   `json_script`, never `json`.
2. Edit `metais.yaml`, `inputs/`, `templates/` and `examples/`.
   `metais help manifest` gives every field of `metais.yaml` with an
   example; `metais help templates` gives the template language, every
   filter, and escaping, a URL component's `url_encode` included. Preview
   with `metais render <dir> --sample --out <preview dir>`.
3. `metais check <dir>` — every defect, without data.
4. `metais test <dir>` — renders each example and compares it with its
   `expected/` outputs; `metais test <dir> --update` records them.
5. `metais pack <dir>` — check, test, and write `<name>-<version>.metais`.

To change a packed package: `metais unpack report.metais --out <dir>`,
edit, then `check`, `test` and `pack`.

## Machine output

`--json` on any command prints exactly one JSON document on standard
output: `{"format", "ok", "findings", "summary", "result", "next"}`.
`ok` is false when any finding is an error; each finding has a `code`,
a `message` and a `hint`. `metais help json` lists every format.

## When stuck

- `metais help` — the commands and both paths.
- `metais help <command>` — a command's operands, flags, refusals and
  examples.
- `metais help inputs` — supplying inputs, and which source wins.
- `metais help templates` and `metais help manifest` — writing templates
  and `metais.yaml`.
- `metais help refusals <command>` — every code a command can report, with
  the next step.
- A finding's `hint` says what to do; its code is stable.

than the version in the last line, `metais skill --dry-run` says whether to
refresh it.

before each line break. {{ inputs.note | newline_to_br }} gives line 1
\nline 2 remove Removes every occurrence of a text. {{ "a-b-c" | remove: "-" }} gives abc remove_first Removes the first occurrence. {{ "a-b-c" | remove_first: "-" }} gives ab-c remove_last Removes the last occurrence. {{ "a-b-c" | remove_last: "-" }} gives a-bc replace Replaces every occurrence of a text with another. {{ "a-b-c" | replace: "-", "+" }} gives a+b+c replace_first Replaces the first occurrence. {{ "a-b-c" | replace_first: "-", "+" }} gives a+b-c replace_last Replaces the last occurrence. {{ "a-b-c" | replace_last: "-", "+" }} gives a-b+c split Splits a string into an array at each separator. {{ "a,b,c" | split: "," | join: " " }} gives a b c truncate Cuts a string to a number of characters, the ellipsis (... unless given) included. {{ "abcdefgh" | truncate: 6 }} gives abc... truncatewords Keeps a number of words, then the ellipsis (... unless given). {{ "one two three" | truncatewords: 2 }} gives one two... a float adds as the decimal it is written as. {{ 0.1 | plus: 0.2 }} gives 0.3 minus Subtracts. {{ 5 | minus: 7 }} gives -2 times Multiplies. {{ 3 | times: 1.5 }} gives 4.5 divided_by Divides; two integers give the quotient rounded down. {{ 7 | divided_by: 2 }} gives 3 modulo The remainder of the division rounded down. {{ -7 | modulo: 2 }} gives 1 at_least The larger of the value and the argument. {{ 3 | at_least: 5 }} gives 5 at_most The smaller of the value and the argument. {{ 3 | at_most: 2 }} gives 2 Arrays: size The length of a string, array or object; # The invoice

The header of one invoice: who bills whom, its number and dates, and the
terms every amount is computed on. Take each value from the seller's
records; none of them is computed.

- **number** is the seller's invoice number, unique among their invoices.
- **issue_date** is the day the invoice is issued; **due_date**, when
  given, the day payment is due. Both are `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- **currency** is the ISO 4217 code every line item's price is in. The
  invoice prints amounts with two decimal places, so a currency without
  cents, such as JPY, prints `.00`.
- **tax_rate** is the percentage charged on the subtotal, after every
  discount line. Leave it out, or give 0, when no tax is charged: the
  invoice then prints no tax line. **tax_label** names it (VAT, GST).
- **seller** and **bill_to** each hold a **name**, and optionally an
  **address** (one line per line of the address), an **email** and a
  **tax_id**.
- **payment_terms** and **notes** are printed at the foot, as written.

  - optional: due date, tax rate, a name for the tax (such as "VAT"), payment terms and notes;
  - seller and customer each need a name, and can also have an address, email and tax ID.
- **`line_items`** (JSON, YAML or CSV): each row has `description`, `quantity` and `unit_price`, plus an optional `unit` such as "hours". The CSV header is `description,quantity,unit,unit_price`.

**How the totals work:**
- Each line is quantity × unit price, rounded to the cent. The subtotal adds up the lines, and tax is the subtotal × the rate, rounded. All the arithmetic is done in whole cents, so no floating-point error creeps in.
- Fractional quantities are allowed (7.5 hours). A negative unit price is a discount or credit, and tax is charged on what's left after it.
- Amounts print like `1,096,669.89`, with a minus sign for negatives. With no tax rate, the tax line is left out.
- Every value is HTML-escaped.

**How I checked it:** the example (`invoice/examples/basic`) feeds its line items in as CSV and covers thousands separators, a quantity that rounds (7.5 × 145.33 → 1,089.98), a discount, 8.25% tax and a description containing `&` and `<`. The rendered totals match the ones I worked out by hand (subtotal 1,013,089.97, tax 83,579.92, due 1,096,669.89). Renders from generated sample data with very large amounts also came out formatted correctly.

**Limits:**
- Amounts always show two decimal places, so a currency without cents like JPY prints `.00`.
- Quantities don't get thousands separators.
- There's one tax rate for the whole invoice, not one per line.

**To use it:**
```
metais render invoice-0.1.0.metais --data <dir with invoice.json + line_items.csv> --out <new dir>
metais render invoice-0.1.0.metais --sample --out <new dir>   # preview with made-up data
```
To change it, edit `invoice/`, then run `metais pack invoice`. It writes the new `.metais` into whatever directory you run it from.
